workingTreeState: Inventory source is committed Go code at sourceCommit; uncommitted tracked changes are docs-only and excluded from Go AST traversal. Ignored .artifacts evidence is excluded.

method.baselineGraph: preserved docs/validation/clean-architecture-baseline.json records baseline sourceCommit e116e5c; package/edge inventory is reused, while Core metrics are independently recalculated from baseline Git blobs
method.distinctImports: unique production import paths per Core metric, standard library and external modules included; no transitive imports
method.edgeCounts: unique From→To pairs; production uses non-test Go files, testLocalEdges uses test files, testOnlyLocalEdges subtracts production pairs from test pairs
method.forbiddenEdges: same layer rules as internal/tooling/architecture.Check at source commit, evaluated for every current local import edge; test imports are checked too
method.lineCounts: physical LOC counts newline-delimited source lines (including a final unterminated line); nonblankNoncommentLOC counts source lines with a scanner token other than comments/EOF, including string/raw literals and code lines with trailing comments
method.sourceTraversal: Go AST parsing of every .go file under internal/, cmd/, tools/, examples/, integration/, experiments/, benchmark/, including _test.go and platform-suffixed/build-tagged files; no build selection or compilation
method.termLexiconCountAlgorithm: Production Core Go files only; AST identifiers are matched case-insensitively against exact whole names and camel-case/underscore fragments; comment and STRING/CHAR BasicLit text uses case-insensitive non-alphanumeric boundaries. The categories are counted separately to avoid substring false positives such as Signature matching Git. Opaque literals include import paths and embedded compatibility tokens; no prose/YAML files are scanned.

Path and line are generic diagnostic provenance labels; retain only as opaque values and never interpret them as filesystem location or load source bytes.

normalizedCorePreconditions: Host authoring frontend decodes source syntax, activates only selected vocabularies, validates source envelopes, normalizes each resource once, and supplies explicit descriptors, relationships, snapshots, configuration digests, source provenance, exceptions, and policy dates.
Core receives normalized Resource.Data as the single canonical value; it does not parse YAML, infer Project/Package policy, acquire repository bytes, read a clock, or choose providers.
Package and source path/line values are opaque identity/provenance labels; Core does not interpret their filesystem or package-activation meaning.
Where legacy subject-digest field ordering matters, Host supplies GraphKey-to-encoding bytes explicitly; Core copies and hashes those bytes without decoding or branching on them.
